triage_candidates.statement: tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py:182 cli_current_text() calls subprocess.run([sys.executable, ENGINE, ..., 'current'], capture_output=True, text=True) with NO explicit encoding -- the identical missing-encoding defect this gate (g3fix2) fixed in tests/test_mcp_identity.py and tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py, but this file was explicitly NOT in the g3-implementer-handoff-utf8.md scope list (scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, tests/test_mcp_identity.py, tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py only). checklist_engine.py's own _utf8_stdio() already pins the CLI child's stdout to UTF-8 on write, so the CLI subprocess emits genuine raw multi-byte UTF-8 bytes for its rendered 'ACTIVE <id> [<status>] -- <imperative>' line (unlike the MCP door's JSON-RPC responses, which are ASCII-safe by construction via json.dumps' default ensure_ascii=True); on Windows this parent-side read would decode those raw bytes with the platform cp1252 default and mojibake exactly like 'testerâ€”café', breaking the ACTIVE_LINE_RE match this file's extract_imperative() requires -- this is very likely the literal file/line the handoff's pasted CI failure trace ('projection for g1-implement has an ACTIVE line that does not match the expected shape ... â€”') originates from. Verified locally: this exact reasoning was confirmed by reproducing the analogous bug in tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py via PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 (see this plan's m1 evidence); the Windows-CI claim for THIS specific file is reasoned by symmetry, not independently reproduced (cannot run Windows). Recommend Commander decide: amend g3fix2's scope by one file and add 'encoding=utf-8' to this one subprocess.run call, or route as an immediate follow-up issue -- either way, until it lands, the DC4 population test may still fail with mojibake on Windows CI even after this fix merges.

why_trail.why: read global-crew.md, global-everyone.md, windows.md, g3-implementer-handoff-utf8.md in full, scripts/mcp_spine_server.py's stdio loop (line ~528-573), checklist_engine.py's own _utf8_stdio() (~43-55, module-level, stdout/stderr only) and load()/save() (~174-209, both already explicit encoding=utf-8), test_mcp_identity.py's ServerInstance Popen (~118-122, text=True no encoding), test_mcp_spine_server.py's 4 Popen/subprocess.run text=True call sites (McpRpcClient ~141-145, _cli_current ~224-226, CLI-refusal ~376-380, var-expansion ~466-469), and test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py's cli_current_text (~180-182, same defect, NOT in handoff scope). Key finding: json.dumps ensure_ascii=True (default, used throughout the JSON-RPC layer) ASCII-escapes the protocol payload, so the reachable defect is specifically sys.stdin decoding a raw (non-ASCII-escaped) request from a real non-Python MCP client, not the Python test clients which never emit raw non-ASCII bytes.
